title: Tailoring Vaccine Messaging with Common-Ground Opinions
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the ability of Large Language Models to generate tailored vaccine messaging by aligning responses with Common-Ground Opinions (CGOs), one of which included the topic of religion. It measured the quality of these tailored responses to determine if using religious opinions as a basis for common ground could effectively address specific vaccine concerns.
findings: The study found that using 'religion' as a common-ground opinion topic generally resulted in lower quality scores for tailored vaccine messaging, likely because controversial or polarized topics are harder to use to establish common ground. However, the models were still able to generate highly effective and strong responses in specific contexts, such as tailoring an 'evangelical Christian' identity (appealing to loving one's neighbor and protecting vulnerable populations) to address concerns regarding the direct transmission of the virus from the vaccine.
